comment: Full metal parity for tool heads and the tools built from them. Vanilla stops at nine metals; every metal Haft carries material stats for is added here, so a metal that can be a handle or a binding can also be a head. Several are far too soft to be useful tools - a lead axe is a decoration, not an upgrade - and that is deliberate: the stats already price them honestly, and players who build for looks get the full set. Textures need no work, as every toolhead resolves its metal through block/metal/ingot/{material} and vanilla ships an ingot texture for all of them; shapes reuse the existing copper or iron models.
The finished tools take the same metals, or a head could be smithed and never hafted.
Without these the heads exist but nothing can smith them. Same metal list as above.

Only recipes whose OUTPUT item is extended above appear here. Tongs were dropped: tongsmetal needs block/metal/sheet-plain/{metal}1 art that vanilla ships for only a few metals, so the item cannot take the new ones and its recipe would smith a nonexistent tongsmetal-standard-<metal>.

Rewrites the whole map because the new rule has to sit BEFORE the '*' fallback - first match wins, and an add would append after it. Vanilla sends any metal outside its hardcoded nine to block/stone/rock/{material}1, a stone path that does not exist for a metal, which logged one 'Texture asset not found' per metal per variant.

Vanilla sends any metal outside its hardcoded nine to block/stone/rock/{material}1, a stone path that does not exist for a metal, which logged one 'Texture asset not found' per metal per variant.

Uses the same three-step the Uranium Expanded mod uses for its own heads: addmerge the per-metal keys into shapeByType, remove the '*' wildcard, then addmerge it back so it is re-appended LAST. Vanilla ships the wildcard as the final key and first match wins, so keys merely added after it never matched and every new metal fell through - to a stone model on most heads, and to the assembled tool on the pickaxe. Model only; the colour still comes from each metal's own ingot texture, exactly as it does for the uranium heads.

bladehead-falx-* already matched the new metals but resolved to item/tool/blade/falx/{metal}, a file vanilla ships only for its own nine. Explicit keys are merged in, then the pattern is removed and re-added so it lands after them.
wrench has no shapeByType at all, only a plain shape:, so the map is created here with the wildcard last.

Multi-part rendering counterpart to the vanilla-model blocks above. Those assign each new metal a vanilla shape - which for several tools is the ASSEMBLED tool including its handle, not a bare head - and carry no condition, so with Haft's part rendering on they overrode the head models Haft's own patches/partshapes/ set up and re-appended a vanilla '*' fallback over Haft's. Each vanilla-model block is now gated to rendering:false and mirrored here at rendering:true against haft:item/parts/<tool>/heads/<tier>. Tiering follows the rule already in patches/partshapes/: the advanced-era metals take 'advanced', the rest take the tool's non-advanced tier - 'normal' on axe, hammer and pickaxe, which are the only tools that have one, and 'simple' elsewhere. Each tool's own '*' fallback is restored, which is 'nonmetal' on axe, hoe, knife and shovel and 'simple' on the tools that ship no nonmetal head.

Durability for the new metals. Vanilla's durabilitybytype lists one key per metal and ships NO '*' fallback, so every metal added above was created with durability 0 - and with no durability there is nothing for Haft to derive its part stats from, which is why none of the new tools carried stats. Values come from a least-squares power-law fit of durability against each metal's hardness in config/haft/stats/materials/metals-vanilla.json, fitted per tool against that tool's OWN vanilla metals so each stays on its own scale. Gold and silver are excluded from the fit: both sit at hardness 0.55 yet vanilla gives scythe-gold 15 and scythe-silver 187, so they are priced by rarity rather than hardness and including them flattened the curve enough to put titanium below steel. No vanilla value is modified - only the new keys are added.
